newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-BOAVISTA FINED BECAUSE OF COIN-THROWING FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOAVISTA FINED BECAUSE OF COIN-THROWING FANS.

text.p: Portuguese side Boavista were fined 50,000 Swiss francs ($35,000) on Monday for failing to control their fans during a UEFA Cup match against Internazionale Milan.
The fans pelted a UEFA official with coins during the third round second leg match in Boavista's home city of Porto in December.
Boavista lost the match 2-0 and the tie 7-1 on aggregate.
UEFA, European soccer's governing body, said it had taken previous crowd trouble involving Boavista supporters into account when imposing the fine.
Belgian side Brugge and Germany's Schalke were fined 30,000 Swiss francs ($21,000) each because of crowd trouble at their third round second leg tie in Germany on the same night.
And AC Milan and Paris St Germain were fined 30,000 Swiss francs ($21,000) each after their fans set off fireworks during European matches.
